At **[21:29]**, the professor said: "In the demo I set contamination to 0.05, so the model flags the top five percent of points as anomalies. Set it too high and you start flagging normal data."

This means that if the contamination value is set too high, the model will incorrectly classify normal (non-anomalous) data points as anomalies.
